study_label: Auditory peripersonal space in humans. (a)
title: Auditory peripersonal space in humans.
experiment_label: Experiment 1 — right-side front/back × near/far × sound type
auditory_stimulus: Static free-field wideband white-noise bursts and 1.5-kHz pure tones, level-adjusted to 70 dB at the ear and emitted by a 0.3-W, 8-ohm loudspeaker under sensor/switch control; reusable source waveforms are not supplied.
trajectory_kinematics: Static right-front and right-back sources at 20 or 70 cm from the head, ear level and 45 degrees from the sagittal plane; sound lasts for the tactile contact (brief, under 1 s), so motion speed is not applicable.
trial_sequence: One tactile-only baseline condition plus eight cross-modal blocks (2 sound types x front/back x 20/70 cm). Each 40-trial block used 10 single-left, 10 single-right, 10 bilateral/simultaneous and 10 no-stimulation rows in the same pseudorandom order; the full protocol ran twice.
task_response: After an experimenter attention prompt, participants verbally reported left, right, both, or none after each event, regardless of modality.
jitter_iti_policy: No ITI, inter-trial interval, jitter value, or distribution was recovered after the main-PDF, targeted, fallback, and supplement-route checks.
soa_schedule: Cross-modal sound and touch were simultaneous (nominal 0-ms SOA); there was no varied SOA ladder.
tactile_target: Brief light contact under 1 s with a 1-cm² touch-sensitive sensor on the lateral neck behind the ear, below the mastoid process.
baseline_trial_contract: Tactile-only switch-off baseline with the same manual contact timing: one 40-trial condition x two protocol runs = 80 baseline-block trials (60 tactile-present and 20 no-stimulation).
catch_trial_contract: No-stimulation rows required a 'none' report: 9 conditions x 10 no-stimulation trials x 2 protocol runs = 180, of which 160 were in cross-modal blocks and 20 in tactile-only baseline blocks.
repetition_allocation: Nine condition blocks, each with 10 repetitions of four trial types, repeated in two complete protocol runs: 9 x 40 x 2 = 720 trials per participant (640 cross-modal-block trials and 80 baseline-block trials).
block_order_contract: Nine condition-specific 40-trial blocks per protocol, with condition-block order randomized across sessions and participants; the complete protocol was repeated twice, yielding 18 blocks.

title: Auditory peripersonal space in humans.

trajectory_kinematics: Static left-back sources at 20 and 70 cm from the head, ear level and 45 degrees from the sagittal plane; sound lasts for brief tactile contact and has no movement speed.
trial_sequence: Two cross-modal white-noise condition blocks (left-back 20 and 70 cm), each retaining the 40-trial, four-row structure and pseudorandom trial order used in Experiment 1.
task_response: After an experimenter attention prompt, participants verbally reported left, right, both, or none after each event, regardless of modality.
jitter_iti_policy: No ITI, inter-trial interval, jitter value, or distribution was recovered after the main-PDF, targeted, fallback, and supplement-route checks.
soa_schedule: Cross-modal sound and touch were simultaneous (nominal 0-ms SOA); there was no varied SOA ladder.
tactile_target: Brief light contact under 1 s with a 1-cm² touch-sensitive sensor on the lateral neck behind the ear, below the mastoid process.
baseline_trial_contract: Experiment 2 is described as two added cross-modal condition blocks; no experiment-specific tactile-only baseline block is reported.
catch_trial_contract: No-stimulation rows within the two 40-trial cross-modal blocks required a 'none' report: 2 blocks x 10 = 20.
repetition_allocation: Two distance conditions x 40 trials each = 80 Experiment 2 trials, retaining 10 repetitions of each of the four trial types per condition.

study_label: Dynamic sounds capture the boundaries of peripersonal space representation in humans.
title: Dynamic sounds capture the boundaries of peripersonal space representation in humans.
auditory_stimulus: Stimulus type: Pink-noise auditory samples at 44.1 kHz. | Source provenance: SoundForge 4.5 shaped two identical pink-noise samples for the two loudspeakers; exact source audio file is not reported. | Auditory conditions: IN/approaching and OUT/receding sounds. | Gain envelope: IN: exponential rise 55 to 70 dB SPL; OUT: exponential fall 70 to 55 dB SPL; near/far speaker intensities mirror each other. | Renderer or apparatus: Two physical loudspeakers, SoundForge-generated pink-noise envelopes, audiometer SPL calibration, C.I.R.O. software control.
trajectory_kinematics: Trajectory path: Near speaker on table by the right hand; far speaker on floor about 100 cm from near speaker; IN far-to-near, OUT near-to-far. | Stimulus duration: Sound duration 3000 ms, preceded and followed by 1000 ms silence. | Stimulus speed: No explicit speed reported; nominal apparent path is about 100 cm over 3000 ms, roughly 0.33 m/s, under mirrored exponential intensity fades. | Trajectory count: Two auditory trajectories: IN approaching and OUT receding. | Gain envelope: IN: exponential rise 55 to 70 dB SPL; OUT: exponential fall 70 to 55 dB SPL; near/far speaker intensities mirror each other. | Renderer or apparatus: Two physical loudspeakers, SoundForge-generated pink-noise envelopes, audiometer SPL calibration, C.I.R.O. software control.
trial_sequence: Trial rows families: IN and OUT audio-tactile target trials across T0-T6 plus auditory-only catch trials. | Task sequence rules: Participants said TAH to tactile targets as fast as possible while ignoring sounds; calibration repeated after omissions or catch false alarms. | Condition intermixing: Sound condition, tactile timing, and auditory-only catch trials were randomly combined/intermingled in the main experiment.
task_response: Task sequence rules: Participants said TAH to tactile targets as fast as possible while ignoring sounds; calibration repeated after omissions or catch false alarms.
jitter_iti_policy: Iti jitter policy: Fixed 1000 ms silence before and after each 3000 ms sound; no variable ITI/jitter distribution reported.
soa_schedule: Soa table: T1 300 ms, T2 800 ms, T3 1500 ms, T4 2200 ms, T5 2700 ms after sound onset; T0/T6 baseline timings also included.
tactile_target: Tactile stimulus: Right-index electrical tactile pulse via DS7A Digitimer and Neuroline electrodes; single rectangular monophasic pulse, 100 us, individually set above threshold, 60-90 mA tested range.
baseline_trial_contract: Baseline strategy: Unimodal tactile baseline condition without concurrent sound, implemented during pre-sound and post-sound silence periods. | Baseline timing: T0 at 300 ms from trial start, before sound onset; T6 at 4600 ms from trial start, after sound administration. | Baseline count: T0 and T6 produce 32 baseline/unimodal tactile target trials total: 2 timings x 2 sound-condition trial contexts x 8 repetitions.
catch_trial_contract: Catch trial type: Auditory-only catch trials with no tactile stimulation. | Catch count: Seventy-six auditory-only catch trials in the main experiment; calibration used 5 catches intermingled with 10 tactile stimuli.
repetition_allocation: Repetitions per tactile soa condition: Eight target trials for each temporal delay T0-T6 for each sound condition IN and OUT. | Total trial count: One hundred eighty-eight main-task trials total: 112 tactile-target trials plus 76 auditory-only catch trials.
block_order_contract: Blocked or random order: Randomized/intermingled trials equally divided into two blocks of about 8 minutes each. | Block count: Two blocks, about 8 minutes each. | Condition intermixing: Sound condition, tactile timing, and auditory-only catch trials were randomly combined/intermingled in the main experiment. | Total trial count: One hundred eighty-eight main-task trials total: 112 tactile-target trials plus 76 auditory-only catch trials.

study_label: Extended multisensory space in blind cane users.
title: Extended multisensory space in blind cane users.
auditory_stimulus: Stimulus type: Auditory stimuli were 150 ms bursts of white noise. | Source provenance: Sounds were generated by two identical loudspeakers; phono-spectral waves were recorded by computer to verify equal sounds at the origin. | Auditory conditions: Near versus far sound location was crossed with weak target, strong nontarget, and sound-only catch rows; tool state was manipulated in separate cane/handle/training blocks. | Gain envelope: Near and far sounds were equalized to 70 dB at the participant's ear; sounds were also checked for equality at origin. | Renderer or apparatus: Two identical loudspeakers placed near and far from the stimulated hand; XGen software controlled stimulus presentation and response recording.
trajectory_kinematics: Trajectory path: Near sound was close to the stimulated right hand; far sound was on the floor about 125 cm from the hand, corresponding to average cane length and the fixed cane-tip location. | Stimulus duration: Auditory white-noise bursts lasted 150 ms. | Stimulus speed: No looming or moving auditory stimulus was used; near and far sounds were static speaker locations. | Trajectory count: Two static auditory positions/conditions: near the stimulated hand and far on the floor near the cane tip. | Gain envelope: Near and far sounds were equalized to 70 dB at the participant's ear; sounds were also checked for equality at origin. | Renderer or apparatus: Two identical loudspeakers placed near and far from the stimulated hand; XGen software controlled stimulus presentation and response recording.
trial_sequence: Trial rows families: Rows/families were weak tactile target plus near/far sound, strong tactile nontarget plus near/far sound, and sound-only catch trials. | Task sequence rules: Subjects verbally responded only to weak tactile targets, ignored sounds, received 30 familiarization trials before the experiment, and should not respond on strong nontarget or sound-only catch trials. | Condition intermixing: Near/far sound trials and target/nontarget/catch rows occurred within the task; cane, handle, and sighted training conditions were separate blocked conditions.
task_response: Task sequence rules: Subjects verbally responded only to weak tactile targets, ignored sounds, received 30 familiarization trials before the experiment, and should not respond on strong nontarget or sound-only catch trials.
soa_schedule: Soa table: Near sound and tactile stimuli were simultaneous; far sound onset preceded tactile onset by 5 ms to compensate for the extra sound-travel distance.
tactile_target: Tactile stimulus: Two DS7A Digitimer constant-current stimulators delivered weak target and strong nontarget electrical stimuli through Neuroline electrodes on the upper side of the right index finger; intensities were calibrated to about 90% and 100% perception.
baseline_trial_contract: Baseline strategy: No separate tactile-only baseline is reported; the task estimates PPS effects from near-versus-far sound comparisons across handle/cane/training conditions. | Baseline timing: No tactile-only baseline SOA schedule was used or reported. | Baseline count: No separate tactile-only baseline trials are reported.
catch_trial_contract: Catch trial type: Catch trials were sound-only no-response trials; results report responses on fewer than 1% of catch trials. | Catch count: Per described task: 30 sound-only catch trials.
repetition_allocation: Repetitions per tactile soa condition: Per described task: 30 weak-target trials with near sound, 30 weak-target trials with far sound, 30 strong-nontarget trials with near sound, and 30 strong-nontarget trials with far sound. | Total trial count: The described task contains 150 trials per administered condition; this implies 300 trials for blind participants across cane/handle and 600 for sighted participants if each listed sighted condition used the same task.
block_order_contract: Blocked or random order: Participants performed cane and handle tasks in two blocked conditions with counterbalanced order; sighted subjects had two additional cane-training blocks immediately after and 1 day after training. | Block count: All participants completed cane and handle blocked conditions; sighted participants also completed cane blocks immediately after 10 min training and 1 day after training. | Condition intermixing: Near/far sound trials and target/nontarget/catch rows occurred within the task; cane, handle, and sighted training conditions were separate blocked conditions. | Total trial count: The described task contains 150 trials per administered condition; this implies 300 trials for blind participants across cane/handle and 600 for sighted participants if each listed sighted condition used the same task.
